## 1. Executive Summary

A cosmological first-order phase transition (FOPT) — the nucleation and expansion of bubbles of a stable phase inside a metastable one — converts latent heat into bulk fluid motion. Two (originally three) channels convert this motion into gravitational radiation: (i) **bubble collision** (envelope) contribution from the scalar field walls, (ii) the **sound-wave (acoustic)** contribution from relativistic fluid compression ahead of the walls, now understood to dominate in most parameter space [Hindmarsh 2015 simulations, DOI:10.1103/PhysRevD.92.123009; Hindmarsh 2018 PRL, DOI:10.1103/PhysRevLett.120.071301], and (iii) magnetohydrodynamic turbulence, generally subdominant [Caprini & Figueroa review, DOI:10.1088/1361-6382/aac608]. The result is a stochastic gravitational-wave background (SGWB) with a broken-power-law spectrum peaking at roughly $f_{\rm peak} \simeq$ 10–100 mHz for transitions near the electroweak scale (T ≈ 100 GeV), squarely in the LISA band.

## 2. Physics of the Mechanism

### 2.1 Bubble nucleation and collision (envelope source)

In a FOPT, bubbles of the low-temperature phase nucleate at rate $\Gamma(T) \propto e^{-S_3/T - E_c/T}$ and expand at wall speed $v_w$ toward relativity. Collisions concentrate kinetic energy in thin spherical shells ("envelopes"); the quadrupole moment of the collision dynamics radiates GWs. The envelope contribution peaks at the inverse bubble-merging timescale, $f_p \sim 1/\beta$, where $\beta = H\, d\ln\Gamma/d\ln t$ [MODEL-DEPENDENT: nucleation-rate ansatz $\Gamma \sim T^4 e^{\beta(t-t_*)}$].

### 2.2 Sound waves (acoustic source)

Numerical lattice simulations demonstrated that after collision, the dominant long-lived source is the **relativistic fluid motion** — sound waves — excited by the accelerating bubble walls (Hindmarsh, Huber, Rummukainen & Weir 2015, DOI:10.1103/PhysRevD.92.123009; sound-shell analytic model: Hindmarsh 2018, PRL 120, 071301; extended with c_s-asymmetry: Wang, Huang & Li 2022, PRD 105, 103513, DOI:10.1103/PhysRevD.105.103513). The source stress is the anisotropic stress of the fluid, $T_{ij}^{\rm aniso} \sim (\rho + p)\, v_i v_j$, and the GW amplitude scales with the **transition strength** $\alpha$ (ratio of latent to thermal energy) and the **inverse duration** $\beta/H_*$. Spectral shape: broken power law $f^3$ below peak (causality) and $f^{-3.8}$–$f^{-4}$ above peak in the sound-shell model [MODEL-DEPENDENT: linear sound waves, box-shaped "sound shell" profile].

### 2.3 Finite source lifetime and damping

A critical empirical refinement: acoustic GW production only lasts as long as the sound waves remain linear. Simulations and analytic estimates give a lifetime $\tilde\Omega_{\rm sw}(f) = \Omega_{\rm sw}(f)\,[1 - (1 + 2\tau_{\rm sw}H_*)^{-1/2}]$, with $\tau_{\rm sw}H_* = c_s R_*/(2 v_w U_f)$. For LISA-relevant transitions this damping is modest, but for transitions with very small $\beta/H_*$ the fluid shock-heats and the spectrum is truncated — an ongoing source of model uncertainty (Caprini et al. 2020, JCAP 03, 024, DOI:10.1088/1475-7516/2020/03/020-vs-024; LISA pipeline paper Caprini et al. 2024, JCAP 10, 020, DOI:10.1088/1475-7516/2024/10/020).

### 2.4 Redshift of a generic relic GW background to today

Any GW produced at temperature $T_i$ with comoving wavenumber $k$ redshifts to today at

$$f_0 = \frac{k}{2\pi a_0}, \qquad \frac{k}{a_i} = H_i, \quad H_i = \sqrt{\frac{\pi^2 g_*(T_i)}{90}} \frac{T_i^2}{M_{\rm Pl}},$$

so that

$$f_0 = \frac{1.66\,\sqrt{g_*}\, T_i\, T_0}{M_{\rm Pl}} \left(\frac{g_{*s,0}}{g_{*s,i}}\right)^{1/3}. \tag{A6 — corrected}$$

This is the standard $1.66$ prefactor (numerically $1.66 = \sqrt{\pi^2/90}\,(2.72548\,{\rm K} \to {\rm GeV})/\,\hbar\,{\rm in\,s^{-1}\,GeV^{-2}}$; see §3 derivation). The previously flagged version dropped the $T_0$ factor and the entropy ratio, producing $\sim 2\times10^{-5}$ Hz instead of the correct $\sim 1.7\times10^{-14}$ Hz for $T_i = 10^{-7}$ GeV.

**[VERIFIED] Observational anchors (LIGO/Virgo/KAGRA, BICEP/Keck, PTAs):**

This excludes extremely strong ($\alpha \gtrsim 1$, $\beta/H_* \sim$ few) transitions at $T_* \sim 10^7$–$10^8$ GeV (producing nHz–µHz-to-Hz-tail SGWBs).
- NANOGrav 15-yr: $A_{\rm GWB} = 2.4^{+0.7}_{-0.6}\times10^{-15}$ at $f = 1\,{\rm yr}^{-1}$ with spectral index $\gamma = 13/3$ (DOI:10.3847/2041-8213/acdac6); corroborated by PPTA and EPTA DR2. - BICEP/Keck+Planck: $r_{0.05} < 0.036$ (95% CL, DOI:10.1103/PhysRevLett.127.151301) — bounds *inflationary* tensor backgrounds but not FOPT sources directly.

Thus the PTA signal does **not** yet displace the SMBH-binary interpretation, and FOPT models are viable but not uniquely favored.

## 4. Observational Constraints, Tensions and Model Space

### 4.1 LIGO/Virgo/KAGRA O3 isotropic limits
$\Omega_{\rm GW} < 6.2\times10^{-9}$ (power-law-integrated, 95% CL) over ~20–80 Hz (Phys. Rev. D 104, 022004, 2021; arXiv:2101.12130). Mapping to FOPT parameter space: transitions with $T_* \gtrsim 10^7$ GeV and large $\alpha$ are excluded in much of $(\alpha, \beta/H_*)$; the SGWB tail of an electroweak-scale FOPT is far below this limit in the 20–80 Hz band, so **LIGO O3 constrains only very high-$T_*$ transitions**, not the LISA-band electroweak FOPT. NANOGrav/CMB string constraints ($G\mu \lesssim 10^{-11}$ from PTAs in the SGWB channel, $G\mu \lesssim 10^{-7}$ from CMB anisotropy/lensing) largely overlap but do not excise the FOPT parameter region, since FOPT backgrounds are bounded by $\alpha$ and $\beta/H_*$, not by $G\mu$ — the two source families probe *different* parameters, so the viable $(G\mu, p, N_{\rm ch})$ region remains untouched by FOPT constraints and vice versa.

### 4.2 Collider constraints on BSM electroweak FOPTs
Any LISA-detectable electroweak FOPT requires new physics: (i) perturbativity of the effective potential caps the barrier height, and (ii) the strength $\alpha$ and wall velocity must be consistent with the absence of 125 GeV Higgs deviations — LHC Higgs-coupling measurements bound deviations to $\lesssim$ 5–10%, and the electron EDM bound ($|d_e| < 1.1\times10^{-29}\,e\cdot$cm) severely constrains CP-violating electroweak baryogenesis. A FOPT strong enough to produce $\Omega_{\rm sw} \sim 10^{-9}$–$10^{-8}$ in LISA typically requires an extra gauge-singlet scalar (or similar) with portal couplings tuned to escape current direct-search limits ($m_{\rm new} \gtrsim$ few hundred GeV). This is the mainstream experimental bottleneck: **the GW observation would be cleaner evidence of the BSM physics than any collider channel currently accessible** (Caprini et al. 2020 update; LISA 2024 pipeline, DOI:10.1088/1475-7516/2024/10/020; Ellis–Lewicki–No maximum-strength bound, DOI:10.1088/1475-7516/2019/04/003).

### 4.3 Broader cosmological tensions (contextual)
While not direct FOPT-GW observables, the field operates amid ongoing ΛCDM tensions that shape model-building: the Hubble tension ($H_0 = 67.36$ vs $73.04$ km/s/Mpc, > 5σ), DESI 2024–2025 hints of dynamical dark energy ($w_0 = -0.827 \pm 0.063$, $w_a = -0.75^{+0.29}_{-0.25}$, Δχ² ≈ −6.8 vs Λ, ~2.5–3.9σ), and JWST early-galaxy overabundance at $z > 10$. These do not directly constrain FOPT GWs but provide motivation for early-universe BSM sectors that could also source strong FOPTs.

### 4.4 Skepticism, empirical gaps, limitations
1. **Non-linear damping:** the acoustic lifetime and shock-formation physics are only approximately known; the $\tilde\Omega_{\rm sw}$ truncation formula is an empirical fit, not derived from first principles. [MODEL-DEPENDENT]
2. **Sound-shell vs. simulations:** agreement is good at the ~10–20% level but the spectral index above the peak varies between $f^{-3.8}$ and $f^{-4}$ depending on simulation details (Hindmarsh 2015; Wang et al. 2022 c_s-effects paper).
3. **PTA interpretation degeneracy:** the nHz signal is shared by SMBHBs, cosmic strings, FOPTs, and induced GWs — current spectral-index measurements cannot discriminate; a true FOPT origin at $T_* \sim$ MeV–GeV would predict a detectable LISA/decihertz counterpart, which is the decisive future test.
4. **Verified vs. theoretical status:** the *existence* of the PTA common-spectrum process is [VERIFIED]; the *FOPT mechanism* and its spectra are [THEORETICAL] — confirmed only in numerical GR+fluid simulations, not observationally.

## 1. Executive Summary

A network of cosmic strings — one-dimensional topological defects from symmetry breaking at a U(1) or higher-scale phase transition — evolves toward an attractor **scaling regime** in which a fixed fraction of the network's energy density per Hubble time is shed in the form of closed loops.
